policy_title: Reform Ofsted Inspections and End Single-Word Judgements
stated: Reform Ofsted inspections and end single-word judgements so that parents get a clear picture of the true strengths and weaknesses of each school, and schools get the guidance and support they need to improve.

source.quote: Reform Ofsted inspections and end single-word judgements so that parents get a clear picture of the true strengths and weaknesses of each school, and schools get the guidance and support they need to improve.

bearing_set.reason: Directly reforming school inspection and reporting affects how school quality is identified, communicated, and improved, with material consequences for school standards and the attainment gap.

membership_note: Single-target policy: the reform of Ofsted inspection reports and removal of single-word judgements is squarely aimed at improving school improvement mechanisms and parental transparency, both core O7 indicators. No material cross-outcome tradeoffs can be pinned to a specific other fundamental with a concrete mechanism and indicator — the contested internal debate (does removing a single-word grade reduce accountability pressure, or improve targeted improvement?) is a within-O7 disagreement about effectiveness, not a spillover to a different outcome.
